correctness.rationale: For each parent v, disjoint child supports give rho_v and exactly diagonal W*W. From the polar formula, the one-step column energy is bounded by a_v^(1-t)(sum_child a_u)^t <= (1-t)a_v+t sum_child a_u for all p>0, including zero columns. The child-sum map Q is a positive l1 contraction by unique parenthood. Thus a_n<=((1-t)I+tQ)^n a_0; Tonelli gives sum_v Q^k a_0(v)=sum_{depth>=k}a_0(v), yielding the binomial tail. Dominated convergence proves zero limit; the Chernoff bound proves the depth-tail rate, while constant finite paths attain energy (L-n)/L. A standalone checker passed 30516 finite assertions, not used for the infinite limit.

originality.rationale: Stanković 2026 Proposition 5.8 treats unilateral path shifts and Corollary 5.9 their direct sums with finite blocks; an explicitly constructed injective, quasinilpotent, noncommuting-moduli branching shift in S_p but in no smaller S_q is outside that direct-sum class and also fails Theorem 5.5 assumptions. Trepkowski 2014 Theorem 4.1 is a one-step formula; Bala 2026 is operator-norm, not same-class Schatten, convergence. The initial-depth binomial estimate and endpoint limit for genuine branching are not implications of these inspected statements. Relevant 2024 inequalities do not identify the iterated limit. Searches for exact and equivalent assertions produced no matching published theorem; residual bibliographic risks remain.

value.rationale: Equal-Schatten-class convergence is a genuine boundary case in Stanković 2026; the explicit quantitative depth-tail law handles all countable rooted trees with arbitrary branching and weights, including injective examples outside the cited finite-block/unilateral-path direct-sum class and outside the smaller-Schatten-class hypothesis of the general convergence theorem. The bound translates vertex-depth distributions into convergence rates and the finite-path construction proves no norm-only rate can hold; these are meaningful structural controls beyond operator-norm convergence.
